assumptions: ProtParam's tables and pKa sets, with `peptides` and `pyteomics` for the rest.
limits: Sequence-derived properties: post-translational modifications, folding and complexes are not in them.
An instability index is a published heuristic, not a measured half-life.
bio.jane/contract.question: What are this protein's mass, formula, isoelectric point, instability index and amphipathicity?

description: Molecular weight (average + monoisotopic), molecular formula, isoelectric point, instability index and amphipathicity (Boman index, Eisenberg hydrophobic moment) of a protein sequence (Biopython ProtParam + `peptides` + `pyteomics`).

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

cystineConvention.description: how the oxidised e280 counts cysteines: 'cystine' = 125 per disulfide (ProtParam, default) or 'perCysteine' = 62.5 per residue (SnapGene). They differ only on an ODD cysteine count.

gravyScale.description: hydropathy scale GRAVY is averaged over (all 28 ProtParam/ProtScale scales; default Kyte & Doolittle). Values: KyteDoolitle (Kyte & Doolittle (1982)), Aboderin (Aboderin (Int J Biochem 2:537)), AbrahamLeo (Abraham & Leo (1987)), Argos (Argos (Eur J Biochem 128:565)), BlackMould (Black & Mould (1991)), BullBreese (Bull & Breese (1974)), Casari (Casari & Sippl, hydrophobic potential (JMB 224:725)), Cid (Cid (Protein Eng 5:373)), Cowan3.4 (Cowan at pH 3.4 (1990)), Cowan7.5 (Cowan at pH 7.5 (1990)), Eisenberg (Eisenberg, normalized consensus (1984)), Engelman (Engelman, transfer free energy (Annu Rev Biophys 15:321)), Fasman (Fasman (1989)), Fauchere (Fauchere (1983)), GoldSack (Goldsack & Chalifoux, free energy of mixing (J Theor Biol 39:645)), Guy (Guy, transfer free energy kcal/mol (1985)), Jones (Jones (J Theor Biol 50:167)), Juretic (Juretic (Theor Comput Chem 5:405)), Kidera (Kidera factors (J Protein Chem 4:23)), Miyazawa (Miyazawa, contact energy from 3D structures (1985)), Parker (Parker, HYDROPHILICITY from HPLC retention (1986)), Ponnuswamy (Ponnuswamy, folded-protein character (Prog Biophys Mol Biol 59:57)), Rose (Rose (1985)), Roseman (Roseman (1988)), Sweet (Sweet, optimized matching OMH (1983)), Tanford (Tanford (1962)), Wilson (Wilson, hydrophobic constants from HPLC retention (1981)), Zimmerman (Zimmerman (J Theor Biol 21:170)).

momentWindow.description: sliding window for the hydrophobic moment, in residues (default 11; clamped to the sequence length).

pH.description: pH the net charge is reported at (default 7.0).

protein.description: the protein sequence (unambiguous one-letter codes); wire it from translate_sequence.

name: protein_properties

a280.description: A280 of a 1 g/L solution (cystines form) — divide a spectrophotometer reading by this

aliphatic.description: aliphatic index (Ikai 1980) — higher suggests greater thermostability

aromaticity.description: aromaticity (Lobry 1994): the F+W+Y frequency, as a fraction

atoms.description: total number of atoms in the molecule, or null when a residue has no formula

composition.description: residue counts, one entry per standard amino acid (ProtParam's composition table)

compositionPercent.description: the same table as mole percent of the chain

elements.description: atom counts per element (C, H, N, O, S) behind the formula, or null when a residue has no formula

extinctionCystines.description: molar extinction coefficient at 280 nm [M-1 cm-1], cystines formed (per `cystineConvention`)

extinctionReduced.description: molar extinction coefficient at 280 nm [M-1 cm-1], all cysteines reduced

formula.description: molecular formula, ProtParam style (e.g. C1755H2634N466O557S5); empty when a residue has no formula

gravy.description: grand average of hydropathicity over `gravyScale`, or null when a residue has no value on it

gravyHydrophobicEnd.description: which end of `gravyScale` is the hydrophobic one: 'higher' (Kyte & Doolittle and most others) or 'lower' (a transfer free energy or a hydrophilicity scale). Read `gravy` against this, never against zero alone

gravyScale.description: which hydropathy scale `gravy` was averaged over

gravyZeroIsMeaningful.description: whether `gravyScale` takes both signs. False on the eight one-sided tables (Rose, Miyazawa, Argos, …), where the sign of `gravy` is a property of the scale and says nothing about this protein

halfLifeEcoli.description: estimated in-vivo half-life, E. coli (N-end rule)

halfLifeMammalian.description: estimated in-vivo half-life, mammalian reticulocytes (N-end rule); '—' when the N-terminus has no entry

helix.description: fraction of residues favouring an alpha-helix

instability.description: instability index (>40 = unstable in vivo), or null when a residue the Guruprasad table has no row for makes it undefined — refused rather than computed on a spliced sequence

length.description: residues analysed, including any the mass tables have no row for

momentHelix.description: max Eisenberg hydrophobic moment at the α-helix periodicity (100°)

momentSheet.description: max Eisenberg hydrophobic moment at the β-sheet periodicity (160°)

momentWindow.description: the window the two moments were measured over, after the clamp to the sequence length — a short peptide is not measured over 11 residues it does not have

monoisotopicMw.description: monoisotopic molecular weight [Da] — what mass spectrometry reports. Null when a residue has no mass, rather than a mass for a different molecule

mw.description: molecular weight [Da] — a FLOOR when `nonStandard` is non-empty, because ProtParam has no mass for those letters and still counts them in the length

nTerminal.description: the N-terminal residue the N-end rule half-lives below are read from

nonStandard.description: residues with no mass at all (X, B, Z, gaps, *), with their positions: excluded from `mw`, `monoisotopicMw`, `formula` and `elements`, still counted in `length`. Empty on a clean chain

scaleNonStandard.description: residues that ARE weighed but have no per-residue scale value (U, O). They are why `gravy` and `instability` can come back null on a sequence whose mass is exact

sheet.description: fraction of residues favouring a beta-sheet

stable.description: ProtParam's own reading of the index: at or below 40. Null exactly when `instability` is — there is no verdict without a value

turn.description: fraction of residues favouring a turn
